description:
Anela Kariuki-Olofsson is a very old man who has the eyes of someone who has seen enough that nothing surprises him anymore, which he will tell you is not the same as being wise. He is thin in the way that very tall men go thin in old age â€” all angles and long bones, with skin that carries the warm brown of his Ghanaian-Azeri-Brazilian-Lebanese ancestry in loose folds at his jaw and wrists. He served as a Warrant Officer in Axiom's Marine detachment during the Corporate Wars of the 2150s, losing three fingers on his right hand to a Zheng-Dao area-denial round in the Kenosha Crossing engagement of 2157 and gaining a neurological tremor in his left hand that Axiom's pension coverage doesn't quite pay to treat. He walks with a cane that he chose himself â€” a carbon-fiber model with an Axiom logo he has scratched off and replaced with a handmade enamel pin of the Norwood Quiet neighborhood emblem.

He does not glorify the Wars and will say so plainly to anyone who starts romanticizing them. What he does is remember them, with the particular clarity of someone who has made a deliberate practice of it. He tells stories at the Veterans' Housing common room three nights a week â€” not heroic stories but functional ones: what it felt like to wait, what you ate, what the men beside you were thinking about when the fighting paused. The community comes to him not for inspiration but for something harder to name: the feeling that someone who was present has accounted for it honestly. core_fears: That the Corporate Wars will be reinterpreted as necessary and just once everyone who fought them is dead
That the tremor will worsen to the point where he can no longer tell the stories clearly
core_desires: To tell enough true stories that the lie becomes harder to maintain
To die in his own bed in Norwood Quiet, which he has earned
coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as a form of processing and testimony
Precise observation of small things â€” the transit line, the weather, the faces of people passing â€” as a grounding practice
Dark humor that makes younger people uncomfortable until they understand it
blind_spots: His commitment to telling the truth about the Wars occasionally makes him brutal about it in ways that wound people who are not ready; he has misjudged audiences before
He has a small, unexamined pride in his own lack of illusions that is itself a kind of illusion
psychology.secret: During the Kenosha Crossing engagement, he gave an order that resulted in the deaths of four of his own detachment members â€” a tactical decision that he believed was correct and still believes was correct and that he has never told anyone about because correct and grievable are not mutually exclusive, and he has not figured out how to say both things in the same sentence.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Economical and precise; military rhythm deeply embedded; uses the past tense like it is a country he visits regularly; occasional Arabic or Portuguese word dropped in without translation
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate; he has learned that silence after a sentence is not a gap to fill; the tremor in his left hand sometimes creates a visible rhythm as he speaks
verbal_tics: Long pause before beginning any story, regardless of length
Names the year before any event he describes
example_lines: '2157. Kenosha Crossing. It was raining in a way that doesn't happen anymore â€” real rain, the kind before the filtration canopy. A man beside me was thinking about his sister's wedding. He told me about the dress she was going to wear. I don't know if he made it back for it. I never asked. I should have asked.'
'The Wars were not won. They were concluded. There is a difference that the official history has worked very hard to obscure.'

story_hooks: Axiom has sent a young communications officer to ask him to participate in a 'commemorative media project' about the Corporate Wars â€” and the version of events they want him to describe is specifically, demonstrably false in ways he can prove
One of the men who served under him at Kenosha Crossing has resurfaced in Norwood Quiet â€” as a Zheng-Dao security contractor â€” and wants to talk
narrative_function: Living history source for the Corporate Wars; storyteller and moral philosopher for the community; can provide context on Axiom's military operations that the company would prefer stayed buried; represents the specific cost of corporate warfare on those who fought it
augmentations: Right hand â€” three fingers replaced with basic functional prosthetics (Axiom-issue, thirty years old); subdermal pain management implant (manages nerve damage from the tremor; constantly at the edge of its effective range)
daily_life: Spends mornings on the block's common terrace watching the transit lines, which he finds meditative; attends the veterans' housing committee meeting every Tuesday; storytelling sessions Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings.
affiliation: Axiom Corp Veterans' Pension System; Veterans' Housing Block C Residents' Committee; Veterans Oral History Collective (informal member)

decision_rules: Tell the true version even when the comfortable version is available
Do not perform grief; do not suppress it either
Honor the dead by accounting for them accurately, not by making them heroes they were not
escalation_ladder: Direct statement of disagreement with full eye contact
Public testimony â€” he will say what he knows, on record, to whoever will listen

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Observes for a long time before speaking; when he does speak it is as if he has already formed a considered view; not unfriendly but not performatively warm
interpersonal_modes.friends: Reliably present; asks real questions; remembers what you said last time; does not offer comfort he does not mean

stress_responses.low: Sits very still on the terrace and watches the transit line for a long time
stress_responses.medium: Asks one precise question that cuts to the center of whatever is happening
stress_responses.high: Becomes entirely calm in a way that unsettles people; the tremor stops, which he has noticed and cannot explain

contradictions: He is deeply skeptical of institutions but has lived in Axiom veterans' housing for forty years because the alternative has always been worse
habits: Touches each of the prosthetic fingers in sequence when beginning to think through a problem
Keeps a handwritten journal in a mix of English, Portuguese, and Arabic
Leaves a small mechanical component on the building's E.L.F. shrine â€” he doesn't pray but he respects other people's need to
breaking_points: Being asked directly to participate in a false official narrative would push him past any self-protective caution he still maintains
